merger_description:
Retail Employees Superannuation Pty Limited as trustee for the Retail Employees Superannuation Trust (**REST**) proposes to undertake the following passive investments:

* a commitment for limited partner interests in Quinbrook III SCSp (the **Quinbrook Main Fund**); and
* a commitment for units in Quinbrook III (AU) Co-Investment Trust (the **Quinbrook AU Co-Invest Vehicle**), a parallel co-investment vehicle to the Quinbrook Main Fund for Australian investments.

REST is an Australian profit-to-member superannuation fund with approximately 2 million members and around $112 billion in funds under management (as at 30 June 2026).

The Quinbrook Main Fund and the Quinbrook AU Co-Invest Vehicle are managed by Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners (Jersey) Limited and associated entities (**Quinbrook**). Quinbrook is a global investment manager that raises and manages capital to invest in energy related assets and projects, with a focus on the infrastructure solutions needed to deliver the energy transition.

The Quinbrook Main Fund has made investments in solar and storage, battery and grid firming projects across Australia. All projects are currently at the development stage. The Quinbrook AU Co-Invest Vehicle has not yet made any investments.

The Quinbrook Main Fund will seek to invest in project assets and platform businesses at the development, construction and operational stages, across a broad range of energy infrastructure, including energy supply, renewable energy generation, renewable heat and fuels production and energy storage and infrastructure solutions. The Quinbrook Main Fund will target investments in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia. The Quinbrook AU Co-Invest Vehicle will make investments alongside the Quinbrook Main Fund in Australia.

REST has interests in renewable energy related projects and assets in Australia, including in wind farms and green and climate transition related assets.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between REST and the
targets in the development, construction and operation of
electricity generation and battery energy storage systems in
Australia
b. the parties’ combined share in electricity generation and
storage capacity in the National Electricity Market (NEM) is
expected to be low
c. there does not appear to be any substantive change in the
control of the targets
d. there are alternative electricity generation and storage
providers in the NEM and Australia-wide.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
